title: Why a Drying Coffee Drop Leaves a Ring
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. A spilled drop of coffee dries into a dark ring with a pale centre instead of an even stain. The episode explains the mechanism Deegan and colleagues described in Nature in nineteen ninety-seven: the drop's edge stays pinned to the surface, and because evaporation is fastest at that edge, an outward flow forms inside the drop and carries the coffee particles there. It also covers how Marangoni flow can reverse the effect, how elongated (ellipsoidal) particles suppress the ring, and why the problem matters for inkjet printing and medical diagnostic tests.
